correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts hub-blue and hub-white states. With a blue hub, every white component is a rim path and at least two blue rim vertices are exactly what permits endpoint peeling; with a white hub and at least one white rim vertex, the white graph is connected and a first force exists exactly at the middle of three consecutive blue rim vertices. Direct disjoint counting gives the polynomial, and a four-state transfer matrix exactly enumerates cyclic 111-avoiding rim subsets. The packaged verifier independently simulates the PSD component rule and checks every subset through order 14, every coefficient, the trace enumerator, and the basis count.

value.rationale: The minimum PSD zero forcing number of wheels is a standard prior scalar result, so classifying all successful initial sets is a mathematically natural refinement. The answer has nontrivial structure: hub-containing feasibility is cardinality-controlled, while hub-free feasibility is a cyclic forbidden-pattern condition. This yields a closed basis count and the entire forcing-set size distribution rather than a routine restatement of the known minimum.
